sentences.text: Group Inc. and GS&Co. were among the defendants named in a putative class action relating to variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs), filed beginning in February 2019 under separate complaints and consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

The consolidated amended complaint, filed on May 31, 2019, generally asserts claims under federal antitrust law and state common law in connection with an alleged conspiracy among the defendants to manipulate the market for VRDOs.

The complaint alleges the same conspiracy in the market for VRDOs as that alleged in the consolidated amended complaint filed on May 31, 2019, and asserts federal antitrust law, state law and state common law claims against the defendants.
Beginning in 2011, several individual and putative class actions were filed against the Corporation, BANA, and certain Merrill Lynch entities, as well as other banks on the U.S. Dollar LIBOR panel.
All remaining cases are pending in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

Defendants' motion for summary judgment is pending on all remaining claims, brought by individual plaintiffs and one class of plaintiffs who purchased over-the-counter instruments incorporating LIBOR.

comparisons.peer_summary: Plaintiffs in consolidated antitrust and breach of contract actions regarding artificially high VRDO interest rates obtained class certification in September 2023, which defendants appealed to the Second Circuit; Citigroup and others were voluntarily dismissed in November 2023, and the appeal was granted in February 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citigroup are defendants in the same consolidated antitrust class action litigation regarding Variable Rate Demand Obligations (VRDOs) alleging a conspiracy to manipulate or set artificially high interest rates. Both disclosures indicate that the federal antitrust claims survived motions to dismiss while state law claims were dismissed. Both companies report that the district court granted class certification in September 2023, and both disclose that the defendants appealed this certification grant, with the Second Circuit granting leave to appeal in February 2024. Citigroup notes that it was voluntarily dismissed from the case in November 2023.

sentences.text: Group Inc. and GS&Co. were among the defendants named in a putative class action relating to variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs), filed beginning in February 2019 under separate complaints and consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

The consolidated amended complaint, filed on May 31, 2019, generally asserts claims under federal antitrust law and state common law in connection with an alleged conspiracy among the defendants to manipulate the market for VRDOs.

On November 2, 2020, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss, dismissing the state common law claims against GS&Co., but denying dismissal of the federal antitrust law claims.

On June 28, 2022, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss, dismissing the state breach of fiduciary duty claim against GS&Co., but declining to dismiss any portion of the federal antitrust law claims.

The consolidated complaint asserts violations of the Sherman Act, as well as claims for breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duty, and unjust enrichment, and seeks damages and injunctive relief based on allegations that defendants served as remarketing agents for municipal bonds called variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs) and colluded to set artificially high VRDO interest rates.
On September 21, 2023, the court granted plaintiffs' motion for class certification, certifying both an antitrust class and a breach-of-contract subclass.
On February 5, 2024, the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit granted defendants' Rule 23(f) petition to appeal the district court's order granting class certification.
